title: Simple Microfluidic Devices for in vivo Imaging of C. elegans, Drosophila and Zebrafish
protocol: Design the microfluidic structures using Clewin software.
Print the designs using a 65,024 DPI laser plotter with a minimum feature size of 8 μm on circuit board film.
Clean 2 cm x 2 cm silicon wafers with native oxide in 20% KOH for 1 min and rinse in deionized water.
Blow dry the cleaned pieces with nitrogen gas.
Dehydrate the pieces on a hot plate at 120 °C for 4 hours.
Cool down the pieces to room temperature before proceeding.
Place silicon pieces one at a time on the spinner chuck and turn on the vacuum.
Cover silicon surfaces with ~20 μl hexamethyl-disilazane (HMDS) and coat them using a SPIN150 spinner at 500 rpm for 5 sec followed by 3,000 rpm for 30 sec.
Cover silicon wafers completely with ~1.5 ml of SU8-2025 and coat wafers using SPIN150 spinner at 500 rpm for 5 sec followed by 2,000 rpm for 30 sec to produce a photoresist thickness of ~40 μm.

Spin ~1.5 ml SU8-2050 using SPIN150 spinner at 500 rpm for 5 sec followed by 2,000 rpm for 30 sec to obtain a photoresist thickness of ~80 μm suitable for flow layer fabrication for late larval stages of C. elegans and corresponding control layers.
Place the silicon pieces on a hot plate with the SU8 coated layer on top.
Soft bake the coated silicon pieces at 65°C for 1 minute followed by 95°C for 10 minutes.
Allow the pieces to cool down to room temperature before proceeding.
Place the soft-baked silicon pieces on the exposure stage with the SU8-2025 coated surface facing up.
Use the photo mask with design I (L1) and design II (L2) for the flow layer and control layer pattern, respectively, for early larval stages of C. elegans.
Place the photo mask flat against the coated layer.
Expose the soft-baked SU8 wafers to a 200 Watt UV lamp through the photo mask for 15 seconds.
Use the photo mask with design I (L1) and design II (L2) on SU8-2050 coated pieces to fabricate the flow layer and control layer for late larval stages of C. elegans.
Use the photo mask with design I (L1) and design II (L2) for the basal flow layer and control layer, respectively, for Drosophila/zebrafish larvae on wafers coated with SU8-2050.
Expose the SU8 surfaces through the photo mask to a 200 Watt UV lamp for 15 seconds.
Place the exposed silicon pieces on a hot plate with the coated layer facing up.
Post bake the wafers at 65°C for 1 minute followed by 95°C for 10 minutes.
Allow the pieces to cool down before proceeding.
Develop pieces using SU8 developer solution for 20 min.
Rinse pieces in Iso-Propyl Alcohol (IPA).
Blow dry pieces using nitrogen gas.
Place silicon pieces in a desiccator with the SU8 pattern on top.
Coat pieces with 50 μl of trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl) silane vapor in a desiccator for 2 hr.
Prepare 10:1 PDMS by combining 50 g of Sylgard 184 base with 5 g of curing agent in a plastic cup.
Mix the content manually for ~3 min.
Degas the mixture inside a desiccator to remove all air bubbles formed during mixing.
Pour a 5 mm thick PDMS mixture over silicon wafers with SU8 pattern gently to avoid formation of air bubbles.
If bubbles are formed, degas the PDMS on the SU8 pattern in low vacuum to remove all bubbles.
Place silicon wafers with SU8-2025 pattern on spinner chuck and turn on vacuum to hold them.
Cover wafers with ~1 ml of PDMS mix and coat using SPIN150 spinner at 500 rpm for 5 sec followed by 1,500 rpm for 30 sec.
Coat approximately 1 ml of PDMS mix on silicon wafers with an 80 μm SU8-2050 pattern design I (L1, Figure 1B) using the SPIN150 spinner at 500 rpm for 5 seconds followed by 1,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Coat a thick layer of PDMS mix on silicon pieces with an SU8-2050 pattern design I (L1, Figure 1C) using the SPIN150 spinner at 500 rpm for 35 seconds.
Bake PDMS coated silicon pieces and wafers in a hot air convection oven at 50 °C for 6 hours.
Cut out the PDMS piece from the silicon substrate containing the SU8 pattern II using a sharp blade.
Punch a small hole of approximately 1 mm diameter on top of the reservoir connecting the main trap in the PDMS mold using a Harris puncher.
Place the punched PDMS block (containing the 40 μm thick mold for control layer L2) on a plastic tray with the molded side up.
Place the PDMS coated silicon wafer containing the 40 μm thick SU8 design I on the same tray, with the PDMS coated surface facing up.
Insert the tray inside the chamber of the plasma cleaner and turn on the vacuum for 2 minutes.
Turn on the plasma power and lower the chamber pressure until it turns light pink in color.
Expose both surfaces to 18 Watt air plasma under low vacuum for 2 minutes.
Place the punched PDMS block on a plastic tray, molded side up.
Place the corresponding baked PDMS layer on the same tray, flat surface up.
Expose both surfaces to air plasma using the mentioned protocol.
Bake the two plasma-treated surfaces together at 50 °C for 2 hours under gentle pressure.
Cut out the bonded devices from the silicon substrate with SU8 design I.
Punch access holes at the inlet and outlet reservoirs of the flow channel.
Place the bonded PDMS mold on a plastic tray, molded side up.
Clean a glass cover slip (22 x 22 mm, No. 1 thickness) and place it on the same tray.
Expose the bottom PDMS surface of the device and the glass cover slip to 18 Watt air plasma at low pressure for 2 minutes.
Place the two plasma-treated surfaces together with gentle pressure.
Bake them in a hot air convection oven at 50 °C for 2 hours.
Store the device in a clean environment.
Expose a clean glass surface of size 2 cm X 2 cm with 50 μl of trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl) silane vapor in a desiccator for 2 hours.
Spin approximately 1 ml of a 10:1 PDMS mix on the silanized glass surface using an SPIN150 spinner at 500 rpm for 35 seconds.
Bake the PDMS coated glass substrates in a hot air oven at 50 °C for 6 hours with the coated surface facing up.
Allow the PDMS layer to cool down to room temperature before proceeding to the next step.
Punch the cooled PDMS layer using a custom-built sharp metal puncher designed similar to the flow design for Drosophila/zebrafish larvae at the middle of the PDMS, forming the PDMS spacer layer.
Expose both the PDMS spacer layer and the single-bonded block (flow layer and control layer) to 18 Watt air plasma using a plasma cleaner at low vacuum.
Place the two plasma-treated surfaces together.
Bake them in a hot air oven at 50 °C for 2 hours.
Cut the bonded device from the glass.
Punch access holes at the inlet and outlet reservoirs.
Bond the punched device to a glass cover slip using a plasma cleaner.
Produce an immobilization device for first instar Drosophila larvae with a channel height of ~500 μm.
Duplicate the PDMS spacer layer fabrication process for zebrafish larvae with an additional bonding step.
Create a dual layer of PDMS-S to produce a channel height of 900 μm for 30 hpf zebrafish larvae.
Avoid dust particles during device fabrication.
Ensure two plasma cleaned surfaces are completely dust free before bonding.
Store devices in a desiccator when a clean room is not available.
Connect one end of a micro-flex tube to a pressurized nitrogen gas supply regulator.
Attach the other end of the micro-flex tube to the main trap reservoir through an 18 gauge needle glued to the tube.
Use a 3-way stopcock in the middle of the tube connection for application or release of pressure on the membrane.
Fill the tube connected to the PDMS device with a 10 cm column of distilled water before connecting it to the reservoir.
Turn the valve of the nitrogen supply to read 14 psi.
Monitor the membrane of the main trap deflecting towards the flow channel at low magnification of an inverted microscope.
Wait till the liquid front fills the microchannel completely without any trapped air.
Release the pressure by using the 3-way stopcock to relax the membrane to its resting position.
Fill the flow channel with M9 buffer for C. elegans for 10 min before an experiment.
Fill the flow channel with 1X PBS for Drosophila/zebrafish larvae for 10 min before an experiment.
Locate a single C. elegans of required stage on a NGM plate using a low magnification stereo microscope.
Pick a single animal using a small volume of buffer solution into a micro tip.
Push the single organism through the flow channel inlet.
Adjust the pipetting pressure to position the individual animal under the main trap.
Increase the pressure of the PDMS membrane slowly to position the animal against the channel boundary and immobilize it with 14 psi pressure for C. elegans.
Position the immobilized animal at the center of the microscopic field of view.
Use an inverted microscope at desired settings for high resolution bright field or fluorescence imaging.
Acquire single or time-lapse fluorescence images at predefined frame rate.
Release the trap pressure and monitor the locomotion of the animal for 5-10 min at low magnification.
Flush the animal and insert a fresh animal to repeat the above steps.
Wash all the animals from the waste reservoir using distilled water applied using a syringe.
Dry the channel by pushing air using a syringe for future reuse.
